Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.25% to 25,884 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.31% weighted by turnover, against +0.04% for the median stock, a gap of 2.3 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Fischer Medical Ventures Limited rose 6.7% on 89 times its usual volume. NSE asked the company to explain the move, “Significant increase in volume has been observed in Fischer Medical Ventures Limited. The Exchange, in order to ensure that investors have latest relevant information…”.

Shalimar Paints Limited rose 0.5% on 61 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Asian Paints Share Price Highlights: Asian Paints Stock Price History”.

Dhampur Sugar Mills Limited rose 13.2% on 61 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Dhampur, Balrampur, Renuka zoom up to 14%; here's why sugar stocks rallied”.

The exchange has formally asked 1 company to explain today's move: Fischer Medical Ventures Limited. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

What happened
Breaking
How Trump's proposed tariffs for India compare with rival nations
The proposed reciprocal tariff framework targets India's high import duties, potentially raising US levies on Indian goods from an effective 2-3% toward matching reciprocal rates. Higher landed costs threaten export volumes and operating margins for auto component makers like Bharat Forge and textile exporters like Gokaldas Exports. Watch the US Trade Representative's formal product exclusion list to see whether pharmaceuticals and electronics remain exempt.
Reuters Business · +2 others
NSE receives RBI's approval to launch corporate bond index futures
The Reserve Bank of India approved cash-settled corporate bond index futures on the National Stock Exchange, benchmarked against top-rated corporate debt. The product gives mutual funds, insurance companies, and bank treasuries a standard hedge for credit spreads and duration risk without offloading illiquid bonds. Higher secondary liquidity will narrow corporate borrowing spreads, reducing financing costs for capital-intensive power and infrastructure developers.
BS Markets · +2 others
India bonds tumble as Brent tops $95 per barrel, RBI flags food inflation risks
Brent crude crossed $95 per barrel as the Reserve Bank of India warned of persistent food price pressures, pushing domestic sovereign bond yields upward. Costlier crude widens the current account deficit, pressures the rupee, and lifts feedstock costs for paint manufacturers, tyre makers, and oil marketing companies. The upcoming retail inflation print will show whether the price shock delays domestic rate cuts.

US tariffs squeeze profit margins of small Indian medical device exporters - FlipItMoney
US import tariffs are squeezing operating margins for small medical device exporters, but the impact is largely confined to unlisted, private manufacturers. Listed pharmaceutical and healthcare companies derive their export revenue from formulations, bulk drugs, and domestic hospital networks, leaving their earnings insulated from this tariff pressure.
Geopolitics
Dhampur, Balrampur, Renuka zoom up to 14%; here's why sugar stocks rallied
Industry projections indicate India's net sugar production will drop to a decade-low of 26.52 million tonnes following weak monsoon rainfall. Tighter supply raises domestic ex-mill prices, expanding near-term gross margins for integrated producers like Balrampur Chini Mills and Shree Renuka Sugars. The policy risk lies in the food ministry restricting sugarcane diversion toward ethanol production to secure domestic supply.

Telangana aims to achieve 5 GW data centre capacity by 2029: Bhatti - The Hindu
Telangana set a target to build 5 gigawatts of data centre capacity by 2029, up from current negligible operating levels. Executing this target requires heavy investments in grid substations, back-up power, and industrial cooling systems. This pipeline expands long-term order books for electrical equipment makers such as ABB India and Schneider Electric Infrastructure, alongside commercial cooling providers like Blue Star.

Bharti Airtel's data centre unit, Nxtra, committed capital to build a new facility in Guwahati through an agreement with the Assam government. This expansion into tier-two markets deepens Airtel's enterprise telecom revenue base and expands long-term high-margin cloud infrastructure earnings. A secondary market supply glut reduces computing hardware costs for Indian data centres and IT services companies expanding AI deployments. Secondary chip price benchmarks over coming weeks will confirm if lower hardware costs squeeze global cloud provider capex, impacting Indian IT offshore demand.

Persistent US inflation risks delaying Federal Reserve rate cuts, strengthening the dollar index and pressuring global bullion prices. Lower gold prices reduce collateral values for gold loan NBFCs like Muthoot Finance while easing India's current account deficit by reducing import costs. The upcoming US Core PCE price index data will confirm if Fed policy remains hawkish.

Tighter financial conditions put RBI policy decision in focus next week
Indian banking liquidity slipped into deficit, driving a sharp increase in short-term Certificate of Deposit yields ahead of the RBI policy meeting. Tighter liquidity elevates wholesale funding costs, putting pressure on net interest margins for private banks and non-bank lenders. Daily weighted average call money rates will show if the central bank injects liquidity via repo auctions.

Home Loan EMI May Rise! RBI Could Increase Repo Rate in December - Times Bull
Market expectations of an RBI repo rate hike in December threaten to elevate retail borrowing costs across the banking sector. Higher policy rates transmit directly to floating-rate home loans, dampening credit growth for housing finance companies and slowing pre-sales for listed real estate developers. The upcoming monthly CPI inflation reading will confirm if price pressures force central bank action.

High global interest rates narrow the yield differential with Indian sovereign bonds, reducing foreign portfolio flows into domestic equity markets. SBI's renewable energy loan book at Rs 1.24 lakh crore; financed 60 GW capacity: MD
State Bank of India's green loan portfolio reached Rs 1.24 lakh crore, funding 60 GW of capacity, while management highlighted grid battery storage deficits as a structural project risk. Clean energy credit expansion supports wholesale loan growth across state-run lenders and aids capex for listed developers like Tata Power and NTPC Green. Elevated transmission and storage bottlenecks could lengthen project gestation, deferring commissioning and related debt-servicing schedules.

GSK spinoff Haleon eyes billion-dollar Healthkart bet
Consumer healthcare firm Haleon is negotiating a controlling stake in nutrition platform HealthKart at an estimated valuation of $1.2 billion to $1.4 billion. A transaction at that multiple establishes a benchmark private valuation for India's nutraceutical segment. It increases competitive pressure on listed FMCG firms like Dabur, Marico, and Zydus Wellness, which are expanding their direct-to-consumer health and dietary supplement portfolios.
